thesis: Trace the arc of an open landscape at dawn — amber light breathing over earth and water, four-on-the-floor pulse as heartbeat, the whole rig exhaling together in slow organic unison.

artist_branding.summary: Nora En Pure (Daniela Niederer) is a Swiss DJ/producer whose aesthetic is rooted in nature, wide open spaces, alpine lakes, and organic warmth. Her visual world avoids the aggressive neon of standard house — instead: earth tones, warm ambers, soft whites, natural textures. Her label Purified Records and artist brand consistently use golden hour photography, muted natural palettes. The music itself is deep melodic house with piano, lush pads, and driving four-on-the-floor — emotional but never overwrought. Live production favors slow atmospheric haze and warm front-wash over busy movement.
visual_cues: Open landscape / golden hour aesthetic: warm amber-to-gold palette earned by energy, not constant
Nature-organic motion: movers breathe as a unified organism — slow synchronized sweeps, never busy
Piano / chord hits drive accents: key melodic stabs in the 'other' stem should land visible light shifts
Front-wash intimacy: 4BAR as primary wash color foundation, missyees as soft ambient halo
Restraint over spectacle: nothing garish — the lighting should feel like sunlight, not a rave
do_not_copy: Do not reproduce Nora En Pure's specific stage set pieces, festival production design, or Purified Records branded visuals directly.

motifs: Bartók reference: Béla Bartók drew from Hungarian/Romanian folk traditions — earthen, rooted, rhythmic but graceful. Lighting should feel rooted, not floating.
Four-on-the-floor as folk pulse: the kick drum is the heartbeat of the land, not a rave weapon — warm amber on the floor wash on every bar 1

Melodic arc motif: Bartók compositions often move from austere opening to lush middle section to sparse close. Mirror this — sparse amber intro → full warm gold chorus run → stripped-back re-intro → triumphant final run → gentle outro

visual_direction.color_story: Open in deep warm amber-brown (earthy, pre-dawn). First chorus reveals warm gold — the sun cresting the ridge. Breaks strip back to burnt sienna / dim amber. Re-intro at 4:43 is nearly bare — just floor wash and a single mover beam. Final chorus run blooms into full warm gold with pale straw-white accent. Outro fades back through amber to dark earth.
visual_direction.motion_story: All movers move as one breathing organism throughout — slow 4-bar arcs from upstage left to downstage center to upstage right. No independent divergence. Build sections use convergence toward DSC. Chorus uses wider sweeps. Breaks park at DSC and dim. Re-intro: single Sharpy beam at DSC, everything else minimal.
visual_direction.staging_story: 4BAR provides the color foundation (warm amber base across all 4 pars) — this is the 'landscape' layer. Movers are the 'beam organism' above it. Missyees fill ambient sides. NI3K lasers activate only in the final chorus run from ~5:06 onward. No strobe at any point — this is organic melodic house, not techno.

must_include: Warm amber-to-gold color arc as the primary palette — earthen, never cold or blue
Unified mover organism: all movers synchronised at same position and color at all times
Re-intro strip (4:43–5:06): minimal — single beam + dim floor wash only
NI3K lasers only from final chorus run (~5:06+)
avoid: Strobe at any point — this is organic melodic house
Cold or blue color palette — everything should be warm earth tones
Fast or independent mover movements — all motion is slow unified breathing, 4-bar minimum
Saturated neon or rave aesthetics — always muted, warm, natural
